chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and then learned after marrying her that she had committed fornication. He said: If her husband wishes, he may take the dowry from the one who married her off to him, and she is entitled to the dowry for what he made lawful of her private part. And if he wishes, he may leave her. This report is not contradictory to what we mentioned earlier, because he only said: 'If he learns that she had committed fornication, he has the right to claim the dowry from her guardian.' He did not say that he has the right to return her (repudiate her). Nor is it impossible that he has the right to reclaim the dowry even if he does not have the right to annul the contract, because one of the two matters is separate from the other.
ai.seo_question: What are the financial and marital consequences if a husband discovers his wife committed fornication before marriage?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the financial right to reclaim the dowry (*sadaq*) from the wife's guardian and the contractual right to annul the marriage (*faskh*), clarifying that one does not automatically entail the other. This nuance highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that pre-marital fornication serves as a ground for financial compensation without necessarily invalidating the marital bond, allowing the husband discretion based on his preference. The text resolves apparent contradictions in earlier narrations by specifying that the right to claim dowry is conditional upon the knowledge of fornication, whereas the right to return the wife is a separate legal possibility.
